title: Build fails for esp32s3 Echoear target
body:
### Answers checklist.

- [x] I have read the documentation [XiaoZhi AI Programming Guide](https://ccnphfhqs21z.feishu.cn/wiki/F5krwD16viZoF0kKkvDcrZNYnhb) and the issue is not addressed there.
- [x] I have updated my branch (master or release) to the latest version and checked that the issue is present there.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a similar issue and not found a similar issue.

### XiaoZhi AI version.

v2.0.5-3-g01a12b3

### Operating System used.

macOS

### How did you build your project?

Command line with idf.py

### If you are using Windows, please specify command line type.

None (i use zsh on macOS)

### What is the expected behavior?

Project build complete successfully.

### What is the actual behavior?

`FAILED: esp-idf/main/CMakeFiles/__idf_main.dir/display/lvgl_display/jpg/image_to_jpeg.cpp.obj`
or `FAILED: esp-idf/main/CMakeFiles/__idf_main.dir/boards/common/esp32_camera.cc.obj`


### Steps to reproduce.

1. Step: run `idf.py set-target esp32s3` (After cloning repo and run command `source ~/esp/esp-idf/export.sh`)

2. Step: run `idf.py menuconfig`, choose Xiaozhi Assistant -> Board Type = EchoEar

3. Step: run `idf.py build`. After generating the ESP32-S3 image, the build fails with errors (see build log). 

4. Step: Fix it: xiaozhi-esp32-1/main/display/lvgl_display/jpg/image_to_jpeg.cpp: 
line 146:  ESP_LOGE(TAG, "[Unreachable Case] unsupported format: 0x%08x", format);     
line 189: ESP_LOGE(TAG, "unsupported format: 0x%08x", format);
NEED TO CHANGE 0x%08x -> 0x%08lx

5. Step: Run again `idf.py build`. You get same problem: FAILED: esp-idf/main/CMakeFiles/__idf_main.dir/boards/common/esp32_camera.cc.obj

title: Does this tool leave any residue other than autorun?
body: I am writing a program to help people remove malware that abuses `defendnot`. If I only delete the autorun entry but not anything else, will your program have any residue left over (think DLL files etc.)?
author: PPPDUD

[{'user': 'es3n1n', 'created_at': '2025-05-18T22:07:48Z', 'body': "Hello. Yes, this should be enough. You can take a look at the startup.cpp in defendnot-loader/core and use the same code to delete the scheduled task. 
At the same time, though, I don't see any point in a specific tool that purely removes defendnot from the startup as you can just do defendnot-loader --disable, but perhaps im missing something there."}, {'user': 'PPPDUD', 'created_at': '2025-05-18T22:20:48Z', 'body': "> Hello. Thanks for your help.'}, {'user': 'AlexeyVed', 'created_at': '2025-12-09T21:31:29Z', 'body': '@mrousavy I guess the issue should be there. Just not to open a new issue I'm posting it here. What the claude code want you to know:

## Description

NitroModules fails to build on iOS with the following error:

```
error: compiling for iOS 15.1, but module 'CxxStdlib' has a minimum deployment target of iOS 16.0
```

## Root Cause

The `NitroModules.podspec` uses `min_ios_version_supported` from React Native (line 17):

```ruby
s.platforms = {
  :ios => min_ios_version_supported,  # This resolves to 15.1 in RN 0.81.5
  ...
}
```

However, NitroModules enables Swift/C++ interop via:

```ruby
"SWIFT_OBJC_INTEROP_MODE" => "objcxx"
```

This requires the `CxxStdlib` module, which is only available on **iOS 16.0+**.

## Environment

- **react-native:** 0.81.5
- **react-native-nitro-modules:** 0.31.10
- **react-native-mmkv:** 4.1.0
- **Xcode:** 16.x
- **macOS:** Sonoma

## Reproduction

1. Create an Expo project with New Architecture enabled
2. Install `react-native-mmkv` (which depends on `react-native-nitro-modules`)
3. Run `npx expo run:ios`
4. Build fails with `CxxStdlib` deployment target error

## Current Workaround

Add a `post_install` hook in Podfile:

```ruby
installer.pods_project.targets.each do |target|
  target.build_configurations.each do |config|
    config.build_settings['IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET'] = '16.0'
  end
end
```

## Suggested Fix

Update `NitroModules.podspec` to require iOS 16.0 minimum:

```ruby
s.platforms = {
  :ios => '16.0',  # Required for CxxStdlib (Swift/C++ interop)
  :visionos => 1.0,
  :macos => 10.13,
  :tvos => 13.4,
}
```'}, {'user': 'mrousavy', 'created_at': '2025-12-10T15:49:19Z', 'body': "> I'm not sure

well, did you try changing it? in your `node_modules/react-native-nitro-modules/package.json`"}, {'user': 'tensfeld', 'created_at': '2025-12-13T17:27:39Z', 'body': '> > I'm not sure

title: Where is the performance?
body: Also, those models that freely fit and work in llama.cpp do not fit in the ik_llama.cpp, for example, gemma3-4b consumes 70GB of RAM in the ik_llama.cpp and then causes a kill
author: Naster17
comments: [{'user': 'Naster17', 'created_at': '2025-12-23T00:17:19Z', 'body': 'I tried to switch to ik_llama.cpp so that my larger models would work faster, but in the end, even those that worked before no longer fit. Example: ``` ./build/bin/llama-cli -m ~/llama.cpp/qwen3-vl-8b-i-f16.gguf -p "Hi" -t 12 -ngl 1 # cause kill ... ... ... [1] 90762 killed ./build/bin/llama-cli -m ~/llama.cpp/qwen3-vl-8b-i-f16.gguf -p "Hi" -t 12 -ng ``` When im using llama.cpp its performs like 30-50tokens/s '}, {'user': 'magikRUKKOLA', 'created_at': '2025-12-23T01:30:03Z', 'body': "@Naster17 > ``` -ngl 1``` But at the screenshots you're having the ```ngl``` == 10. At the same time the actualy LLama-3.2-1b seem to have 15 layers. So how many layers are you actually offloading to the GPU? 1? 10? In any case, why not to offload all layers to the GPU? What's the point of not to?"}, {'user': 'MrHills-2', 'created_at': '2025-12-23T01:33:59Z', 'body': "Well, in my tests ik_llama.cpp is much, much faster in pp (5x even) and slightly faster in tg (20%). That said the bulk of the difference you see by setting a high -b (8192) and -ub (4096) at high context, and with mixed inference using -ot and -ngl to put moe layers in ram and the rest in VRAM. That's with cuda. Idk about amd. At any rate.. a 4b model consuming 70GB shouldn't be possible. Either it's a bug of you did something odd without realizing. Memory footprint is the same for llama and ik_llama for me. Maybe share your build commands?"}, {'user': 'abc-nix', 'created_at': '2025-12-23T07:26:06Z', 'body': 'vulkan has better support in llama.cpp. Also, I think flash attention is "on" by default in llama.cpp (at least for cuda). Test again with flash attention on.'}, {'user': 'Naster17', 'created_at': '2025-12-23T12:32:10Z', 'body': 'In general, I checked a lot of configurations and builds with vulkan, flash attention etc. And I came to the conclusion that no matter how much memory I allocate to swap for offloading, it will take it all until it leads to kill. Maybe it's memory leaks or something else In terms of performance, I also could not squeeze anything out using wikis and other issues, so far llama.cpp is in the lead in vulkan, although it does not have normal swap offload on the CPU, but at least it works '}, {'user': 'magikRUKKOLA', 'created_at': '2025-12-23T14:56:03Z', 'body': "@Naster17 > In general, I checked a lot of configurations and builds with vulkan, flash attention etc But you **never** mentioned what you were using. The version of the drivers, of the VBIOS, of the OS, of the gcc etc. What were the compilation flags etc. > no matter how much memory I allocate to swap for offloading, i And you're configuring it via the ```-ngl``` parameter? Unclear. That said, I do not have a single AMD GPU so I am unable to test. etc."}, {'user': 'ikawrakow', 'created_at': '2025-12-23T15:51:47Z', 'body': "@Naster17 `ik_llama.cpp` is not the right choice if you want to use Vulkan. There was a point in time where I had made the Vulkan `ik_llama.cpp` build work and be on par, or even slightly outperform, `llama.cpp`. But since then * I have added new optimizations that are not implemented on Vulkan, so will run on the CPU, thus making it slow * The `llama.cpp` developers have significantly improved Vulkan performance, while I have done nothing for the Vulkan back-end I'm basically the only person working on the computation engine, so simply do not have the bandwidth to stay competitive also for Vulkan. `ik_llama.cpp` is good (and faster than `llama.cpp`) for CPU-only, CUDA-only, and hybrid CUDA/CPU inference. "}]

title: Bug: segmentation fault on cache re-use with `-sm graph` AND `--max-gpu 2`
body:
### What happened?

Easy steps:

1. Load model. Test with GLM Air 4.5 and Devstral-2 123B. As a reference - https://huggingface.co/bartowski/mistralai_Devstral-2-123B-Instruct-2512-GGUF/tree/main/mistralai_Devstral-2-123B-Instruct-2512-Q4_K_M
2. Start new chat (`POST /v1/chat/completions`) with `First message` - no cache found, then cached
3. Start new chat with `Second message` - no cache found, then cached
4. Start new chat with `First message` - cache found, segfault

Then same flow with mainstream llamacpp or with ik_llamacpp with `-sm graph --max-gpu 4` works absolutely fine (but slower).

Start command from llama-swap:

```
llama-server
        --model /mnt/data/llm-data/models/mistralai/Devstral-2/mistralai_Devstral-2-123B-Instruct-2512-Q4_K_M-00001-of-00002.gguf
        --jinja
        --port ${PORT}
        -c 128000
        -sm graph
        --max-gpu 2
        -ngl 99
```

### Name and Version

/llamacpp/cpu/llama-cli --version
version: 4055 (59dba9f7)
built with cc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04) 13.3.0 for x86_64-linux-gnu

### What operating system are you seeing the problem on?

Linux

title: Bug: Prompt caching crashing the app with -sm graph
body:
### What happened?

I'm having issues with ik_llama. I'm running
```
ik_llama --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8085 --model H:\AI\llama.cpp\models\GLM-4.5-Iceblink-v2-106B-A12B-Q8_0-FFN-IQ4_XS-IQ4_XS-Q5_0.gguf -a Iceblink -b 3072 -ub 3072 --threads 12 --ctx-size 35840 --n-gpu-layers 999 -ot "[6-9].*_exps.=CPU" -ot "1[0-9].*_exps.=CPU" -ot "2[0-3].*_exps.=CPU" --no-mmap -fa on -sm graph -ts 24,23 -np 1
```
And it works perfectly for the first chat. I can continue and reroll as needed, but as soon as I try to switch to a different chat, I get this:
```

title: Bug: Kimi K2 and Deepseek crash with CUDA error on Turing
body:
### What happened?

Turing cards use CUDA arch 750 as their latest supported version. It appears that the `flash_attn_ext_f16` extension is unable to properly load for this arch version, which results in an immediate crash shortly after the first generation is complete, followed by log spam as shown in the output. 

This only seems to only affect Kimi K2 and Deepseek (possible DS arch issue?); trying with GLM 4.6 causes no issues. A different error occurs depending on what the MLA argument is set to, which might hint towards this being the culprit. The errors did not happen on an older version of ik_llama.

### Name and Version

Hardware: 
`2x RTX 8000 Quadros.`

```
llama-server --version
version: 4027 (5f3485c2)
built with cc (GCC) 15.2.1 20250813 for x86_64-pc-linux-gnu
```
```
llama-server \
    --n-gpu-layers 999 --threads 64 --threads-batch 64 --batch-size 4096 --ubatch-size 4096 --no-mmap \
    --override-tensor "blk\.(0|1|2|3|4|5|6|7|8)\.ffn_.*=CUDA0" \
    --override-tensor "blk\.(9|10|11|12|13|14|15|16)\.ffn_.*=CUDA1" \
    --override-tensor "blk\..*_exps\.=CPU" \
    --ctx-size 42496 -fa on -mla 2 -amb 512 --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --model "Kimi/K2/smol-IQ2_KS/Kimi-K2-Thinking-smol-IQ2_KS-00001-of-00006.gguf" --alias "Kimi K2 Thinking smol-IQ2_KS"
```

### What operating system are you seeing the problem on?

Linux

title: Issue with the JobSystem
body:
Hello, I think there is an issue with the JobSystem. It creates new threads and never destroys them, thus for very large scenes thousands of threads are created, never released, and at one point the system runs out of memory or threads (at least this is what I am guessing). I tried with the Pixar Kitchen scene, with San Miguel scene, and the program crashes at the 1012th bvh build (I have 16 cores on my computer). It's very hard to debug because that much threads considerably slow down the debugger (I use gdb) but I suspect that the crashes I have comes from here (in gdb I can see that 16 threads are created for each build).

Did you receive any complaints about that ? I just got back to work on my pathtracer and I figure that this is the root cause of the crashes I am getting, and the amount of threads there is in the program while I debug stops me from being able to use any debugger, they simply stop working. I'll modify tinybvh and test to see if my intuition is right.

Thank you,
author: romainaugier
comments:
[{'user': 'romainaugier', 'created_at': '2025-08-17T16:58:59Z', 'body': 'I can confirm my intuition, I removed the JobSystem entirely and I can load/build and render the scenes I mentionned without any crash.

The JobSystem should be a static global object initialized once and reused throughout the builds (like a global threadpool), the current implementation attaches one job system per bvh which is very inefficient. Maybe it would be great to have, like for memory allocation, an interface for a threadpool/job-system so that users can provide their own (it could just be an add_task/wait function interface. Most threadpools implement tasks using lambdas (and if not it can be worked around easily). What do you think ?'}, {'user': 'jbikker', 'created_at': '2025-08-18T06:59:52Z', 'body': 'Perhaps a good solution could be a threadlocal static threadpool? That way the BVHs can share those, while the threading remains invisible to the using application, and the library as a whole remains thread safe.

---

Giving it some more thought, the issue does raise some questions: Why are you rebuilding large scenes that many times? Is that regular use in your application or are you doing it to isolate the issue? Typically one would only rebuild a BVH if something changes. The only BVH that is rebuilt per frame is normally the TLAS, for animated scenes. And: When you rebuild, do you perhaps create and destroy the BVH instance for each build? Keeping it around would also prevent spawning additional threads.

I am asking because, although the issue is a real one, it should be quite rare: I would expect it to pop up for scenes consisting of hundreds of large BLASses under a single TLAS.'}, {'user': 'romainaugier', 'created_at': '2025-08-18T08:45:51Z', 'body': '> Giving it some more thought, the issue does raise some questions: Why are you rebuilding large scenes that many times? Is that regular use in your application or are you doing it to isolate the issue? Typically one would only rebuild a BVH if something changes. The only BVH that is rebuilt per frame is normally the TLAS, for animated scenes. And: When you rebuild, do you perhaps create and destroy the BVH instance for each build? Keeping it around would also prevent spawning additional threads.
> 
> I am asking because, although the issue is a real one, it should be quite rare: I would expect it to pop up for scenes consisting of hundreds of large BLASses under a single TLAS.

I am not rebuilding large scenes, but just build them once. Each object in the scene has its blas (and that BLAS is cached until the user clears the cache or the application exit) and each is added to the TLAS via a BLASInstance, that way when the scenegraph changes I just need to rebuild the TLAS if instances changed; but when writing this I realized how inefficient it is for the traversal, so maybe I need to find a way to merge blasses to improve the ray traversal while keeping the flexibility of per object properties (like the masking).

The issue was raised when I was trying larger scenes, with thousands of objects, which meant having to build thousands of BLASses and thus firing a lot of threads. I will review my strategy for organizing the scene in my renderer.'}, {'user': 'jbikker', 'created_at': '2025-08-18T13:54:21Z', 'body': 'I see, that is actually a fine approach. Having lots of BLASses is only bad for performance when their bounds overlap, e.g. when the scene is subdivided in an object per material.

I am currently working on a fix that should alleviate the problem. I think the ````thread_local static JobSystem*```` should work well, combined with suppressing threaded builds for smaller objects (where threading will just yield tiny tasks).

---

The system has been updated as proposed. There is now a pair of static thread_local JobSystem pointers, which are grabbed when a build commences. The grab is needed because the threads of the job system itself would otherwise receive unique pointers, which is not desired. This system should significantly reduce live thread count. It needs a bit of testing, so perhaps you can try if it solves the problems you encountered? Code is in the dev branch.

This has been verified in the speedtest application and the gltf_demo.'}, {'user': 'romainaugier', 'created_at': '2025-08-18T19:12:11Z', 'body': "I just got home and tested, and it works well! Thank you for working on the issue and finding a solution quickly, I couldn't find time for that on my side for now.
Maybe it would be interesting to make the JobSystem a singleton so it would be initialized once and managing itself throughout the life of the application. I am not sure the thread_local is necessary (it would make one job system per thread, firing more threads than physical); but this can be cleaned later.

Thank you again!"}, {'user': 'jbikker', 'created_at': '2025-08-27T11:56:24Z', 'body': "The JobSystem can't really be a singleton, I think: 
At various points BVH builds depend on all jobs to complete. This requires separate queues per build, which is currently enforced by either running builds sequentially (in a single thread) or with a JobSystem per thread (hence the thread_local construct).

---

Closing this one, feel free to re-open if there are problems after all!"}, {'user': 'romainaugier', 'created_at': '2025-08-27T13:10:37Z', 'body': '> Closing this one, feel free to re-open if there are problems after all!

I have been able to test thoroughly during the week-end and everything worked well and as expected! Thank you again for handling this effectively!'}]

A solution that maintains thread safety while sharing threading resources

title: Crash on MacBook M3 due to incorrect aligned_alloc use
body:
tiny_bvh_renderer & co. instantly crash when executed on the M3 MacBook Air (macOS 15.3.2).

The cause seems to be `aligned_alloc` returning NULL for
```primIdx = (uint32_t*)AlignedAlloc( primCount * sizeof( uint32_t ) );```
https://github.com/jbikker/tinybvh/blob/main/tiny_bvh.h#L1876

Man page says
> In addition, aligned_alloc() returns a NULL pointer and sets errno to
     EINVAL if size is not an integral multiple of alignment, or if alignment
     is not a power of 2 at least as large as sizeof(void *).

which seems to happen here for default malloc64.

Aligning the size to 64 with `make_multiple_of` fixes the issue, but there are multiple places where this is necessary.
author: pablode
comments:
[{'user': 'jbikker', 'created_at': '2025-04-02T11:28:32Z', 'body': "Thank you for reporting this. The problem seems to be in the generic aligned allocation block at the top of the file. A proper fix should be:

````
#if defined __APPLE__ || (defined __ANDROID_NDK__ && defined(__NDK_MAJOR__) && (__NDK_MAJOR__ >= 28))
#define _ALIGNED_ALLOC(alignment,size) aligned_alloc( alignment, make_multiple_of( size, alignment ) );
#elif defined __GNUC__
#define _ALIGNED_ALLOC(alignment,size) _aligned_malloc( alignment, make_multiple_of( size, alignment ) );
#endif
````

The use of ````make_multiple_of```` is there for all other platforms but was apparently omitted for Apple. I can't test this myself; could you verify that this solves the problem?"}, {'user': 'pablode', 'created_at': '2025-04-02T16:12:30Z', 'body': 'Yes, that fixes the issue.'}, {'user': 'jbikker', 'created_at': '2025-04-03T06:57:24Z', 'body': 'Awesome, thanks for verifying. I will close the issue then.'}]

  204 | _mm_blendv_ps (__m128 __X, __m128 __Y, __m128 __M)
      | ^~~~~~~~~~~~~
tinybvh/tiny_bvh.h:5602:46: note: called from here

      |                                     ~~~~~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/14/include/smmintrin.h:204:1: error: inlining failed in call to ‘always_inline’ ‘__m128 _mm_blendv_ps(__m128, __m128, __m128)’: target specific option mismatch
  204 | _mm_blendv_ps (__m128 __X, __m128 __Y, __m128 __M)
      | ^~~~~~~~~~~~~

      |                                     ~~~~~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
```

The only way to fix this short of adding `-mavx2` compile option (or changing the source) seems to be to disable SIMD altogether via `TINYBVH_NO_SIMD`. `_mm_blendv_ps` requires SSE 4.1 which is not enabled by default.

Ideally I would expect tinybvh to build as is without errors, either by using compiler-specific "target" attributes to establish the ISA requirements for relevant functions plus cpuid checks, or by disabling the AVX and SSE4.1 codepaths when compiled with gcc/clang without the relevant options like `-mavx2`.

'}, {'user': 'zeux', 'created_at': '2025-03-05T16:09:08Z', 'body': '> Is there a way to detect if -mavx / -mavx2 was specified on the command line?

MSVC does not have this problem (and can be detected via `_MSC_VER`); gcc/clang will set `__AVX2__` define in this case.

> Perhaps the current behavior, where SIMD must specifically be disabled on certain platforms, is a good default.

My opinion is that compiling without errors on stock compiler configuration is a requirement, especially for a single-header library because you do not control the build system.

This isn't mutually exclusive with performance: if you want to use AVX2 regardless, you can annotate the functions that need AVX2 et al (when clang/gcc is used) with "target" function attribute (`__attribute__((target("avx2")))`). This will result in the behavior similar to MSVC: calling these at runtime will fail if the CPU doesn't support it, which can be detected via cpuid.

I'm also not sure if it's a good idea to bundle together AVX2 & SSE codegen: on x64, you can always use SSE2, it's just that future instruction sets need to be opted in via target attribute or compiler flags. While some games are starting to use AVX1 as a minimum requirement, this is rare and AVX2 is not a requirement for any game as far as I know. My recollection is that UE5 currently only requires SSE4.2, and may require AVX1 in the future but doesn't do so yet; don't quote me on that. (note that tinybvh does *not* compile with `-mavx` either, it requires `-mavx2` specifically).

FWIW for my purposes defining TINYBVH_NO_SIMD is enough, I do not plan to use tinybvh in production and don't require SIMD performance so all of the above is purely informational! title: Bug: rotate_sink_tokens kernel not added to CUDA Graph leads to runtime crash
body:
Thank you for creating this educational resource. I’m currently following it to build my own LLM inference implementation. 
I see yalm makes use of CUDA graphs to record and replay kernel launches to reduce CUDA kernel launch overhead. However, I believe there's a problem with how **sink token rotation** is handled.


### The Problem

Relevant code:

https://github.com/andrewkchan/yalm/blob/61068a87bc3bf73c64e7a85e1d009ead6a7b1cb9/src/infer.cu#L809-L832

During CUDA graph creation, `kv_sink` would be 0, so this code path is not executed. As a result, the `rotate_sink_tokens` kernel is **not included in the CUDA graph**. Later, when the KV cache window gets rotated during a subsequent model forward pass, `add_or_update_kernel_node` will try to update a **non-existent node** in the graph, causing the program to crash.

### Steps to reproduce

Use a very small sliding window length to easily reproduce. For example:

```bash
./build/main mistral-7b-instruct-fp16.yalm -i "What is a large language model?" -T 10
```

Output:
```bash
loading data from file: mistral-7b-instruct-fp16.yalm
loading model with dtype: F16
Model active bytes with full context window: 14497898496
Using CUDA
[<s>:1][What:3963][ is:1117][ a:1032][ large:3243][ language:4610][ model:2997][?:29572]
Encoding stats: (8 tokens, throughput: 1.7977e+308tok/s, latency: 0s/tok, total: 0s)



ACUDA error in add_or_update_kernel_node at src/infer.cu:1240: invalid argument (cudaErrorInvalidValue=1)
[1]    1174271 IOT instruction (core dumped)  ./build/main mistral-7b-instruct-fp16.yalm -i  -T 10
```

### Fix

I think putting `add_or_update_kernel_node` inside a conditional block can easily lead to issues like this if not handled carefully.

As for the actual fix, as far as I know, we can't selectively disable kernel nodes in an already-created CUDA graph, so we need to either:

1. create separate CUDA graphs for `kv_sink == 0` and `kv_sink > 0`, or
2. Unconditionally add the `rotate_sink_tokens` kernel to the graph. The kernel itself should return early if `kv_sink == 0`. Maybe also set `gridDim` and `blockDim` to some very small value when `kv_sink == 0` to further reduce overhead.

[{'user': 'andrewkchan', 'created_at': '2025-08-26T06:31:41Z', 'body': 'Thanks for the bug report @stamp711 ! ```
  environment.systemPackages = with pkgs; [
    hyprlandPlugins.hypr-dynamic-cursors
  ];
```

# Find every entry in the store for hypr-dynamic-cursors. For some reason I have like 4 even after garbage-collecting.

$ hyprctl plugin load /nix/store/yg45zrqrp2vlfffiiy1va9x8s783qs0m-hypr-dynamic-cursors-0-unstable-2025-05-08/lib/libhypr-dynamic-cursors.so
```

To be perfectly honest, I don't really know what the "best" way is to use it on nix is, mainly because I don't use nix myself. The flake in this repo has been added by various people who sometimes also update it, but I can't guarantee that it works but for some people it seems to at the moment? Also, the packages on nixpkgs are maintained by some people over there but neither can I guarantee that they work with the hyprland version on nixpkgs.

Maybe important to note is that the `main` branch of this repo targets the `main` branch of hyprland, so on other distros `hyprpm` uses the commits I set in `hyprpm.toml` for different specific hyprland releases, which I guarantee to be compatible. But as I said, I don't know how it is supposed to work on nix if you use a specific release and not just the `main` branch of hyprland.

But yeah I am glad it works now. If you have any ideas to improve/fix the flake feel free to make an MR.

wayland.windowManager.hyprland = {
    enable = true;
    extraConfig = ''
      exec-once = hyprctl plugin load ${pkgs.hyprlandPlugins.hypr-dynamic-cursors.outPath}/lib/libhypr-dynamic-cursors.so

    '';
  };
```"}]

title: Broken with Hyprland v0.51.0-42-gc30036bda
body:
The plugin just seems to not be functional at all.
I use the rotating cursor but it's doing nothing.
Here's my cfg:
https://github.com/nnra6864/Ricerland/blob/Arch/hypr/plugins.conf
author: nnra6864
comments:
[{'user': 'VirtCode', 'created_at': '2025-09-29T13:07:23Z', 'body': "can reproduce

can temporarily be worked around by setting `plugin:dynamic-cursors:ignore_warps` to `false` but I'll have a look at what causes it"}, {'user': 'VirtCode', 'created_at': '2025-10-03T22:32:48Z', 'body': "Yeah it's a bit shit. It's a bug/issue with hyprland's hook system which breaks it on newer versions. I assume all of you are on Arch Linux, building from the AUR? If not please leave a comment, would be important to know.

I seem to have pinned it down that it's related to LTO, but I am not entirely sure. Disabling LTO in the arch build system by adding `options=(!lto)` to the `PKGBUILD` fixes it on my system. Local builds with `-flto` seem to work fine however? So yeah I am still investigating.

I might just disable warp ignoring by default such that it is not entirely broken, as I am quite busy at the moment and have other things to do than debugging why the lto option in the arch build system decides to optimize out the method I need to hook. I hope I can get it done before `0.52`."}, {'user': 'nnra6864', 'created_at': '2025-10-04T08:00:37Z', 'body': "You are correct that I am on arch and using -git from AUR.
It's fine if you are busy, the workaround you provided works flawlessly, although I honestly have no clue what it does 💀 "}, {'user': 'VirtCode', 'created_at': '2025-10-04T08:58:53Z', 'body': 'The `ignore_warps` options was mainly thought for debugging, which is why it isn't documented anywhere really. It is normally set to true which makes the plugin "ignore warps", which means it won't count cursor warps (meaning the cursor "teleporting" to another window when changing focus with the keyboard for example) as actual mouse movement. This makes it look cleaner as the cursor won't e.g. be magnified if switching windows back and forth quickly.

Anyways, I have now disabled it by default on main as a short-term workaround. This way it's not just "nothing happens" when installing the plugin on `-git` on arch.. '}, {'user': 'nnra6864', 'created_at': '2025-10-04T09:10:33Z', 'body': 'I see, thanks a lot for such a detailed response.
Tbh, this should maybe even be an actual config option, some people might prefer that behavior.'}, {'user': 'rharish101', 'created_at': '2025-10-07T23:41:41Z', 'body': 'I installed this using `hyprpm add https://github.com/virtcode/hypr-dynamic-cursors` on Arch Linux, and I face this issue too. I had to use the `ignore_warps = false` option to fix it.'}, {'user': 'VirtCode', 'created_at': '2025-10-12T09:47:48Z', 'body': "Should be fixed now, as I have now disabled LTO when building hyprland alltogether (see https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/pull/11972). So things should now work again with `ignore_warps = true`.

If any of you have some time, it would be nice if you could both update hyprland-git **AND** this plugin, remove the `ignore_warps` (it's enabled by default again) from your config and confirm that it still works. It works on my host but there might be some nuances with other build procedures.

If you are on hl stable, I have recently added a pin which points to a commit where `ignore_warps = false` so it should also work there albeit with no warp ignoring. But when 0.52 releases things will be back to normal."}, {'user': 'nnra6864', 'created_at': '2025-10-14T01:21:53Z', 'body': "I've been trying to test it but I broke Hyprland so bad that as soon as I enable any plugin it just crashes.
Been trying to fix that for over a week, so as soon as I resolve that issue I'll let you know whether the fix actually works."}, {'user': 'rharish101', 'created_at': '2025-10-14T21:52:29Z', 'body': 'Can confirm that it works properly on Arch with Hyprland 0.51.1 when installed with hyprpm.'}, {'user': 'nnra6864', 'created_at': '2025-10-15T23:09:53Z', 'body': 'I can confirm that is works on my end too.
Great work!'}]

body:
Here is my config : 
```ini
plugin {
    dynamic-cursors {

    # enables the plugin
    enabled = true

    # sets the cursor behaviour, supports these values:
    # tilt    - tilt the cursor based on x-velocity
    # rotate  - rotate the cursor based on movement direction
    # stretch - stretch the cursor shape based on direction and velocity
    # none    - do not change the cursors behaviour
    mode = rotate

    # minimum angle difference in degrees after which the shape is changed
    # smaller values are smoother, but more expensive for hw cursors
    threshold = 2

    # override the mode behaviour per shape
    # this is a keyword and can be repeated many times
    # by default, there are no rules added
    # see the dedicated `shape rules` section below!
    shaperule = <shape-name>, <mode> (optional), <property>: <value>, ...
    shaperule = <shape-name>, <mode> (optional), <property>: <value>, ...

    # for mode = rotate
    rotate {

        # length in px of the simulated stick used to rotate the cursor
        # most realistic if this is your actual cursor size
        length = 20

        # clockwise offset applied to the angle in degrees
        # this will apply to ALL shapes
        offset = 0.0
    }

    # for mode = tilt
    tilt {

        # controls how powerful the tilt is, the lower, the more power
        # this value controls at which speed (px/s) the full tilt is reached
        limit = 5000

        # relationship between speed and tilt, supports these values:
        # linear             - a linear function is used
        # quadratic          - a quadratic function is used (most realistic to actual air drag)
        # negative_quadratic - negative version of the quadratic one, feels more aggressive
        function = negative_quadratic
    }

    # for mode = stretch
    stretch {

        # controls how much the cursor is stretched
        # this value controls at which speed (px/s) the full stretch is reached
        limit = 3000

        # relationship between speed and stretch amount, supports these values:
        # linear             - a linear function is used
        # quadratic          - a quadratic function is used
        # negative_quadratic - negative version of the quadratic one, feels more aggressive
        function = quadratic
    }

    # configure shake to find
    # magnifies the cursor if its is being shaken
    shake {

        # enables shake to find
        enabled = true

        # use nearest-neighbour (pixelated) scaling when shaking
        # may look weird when effects are enabled
        nearest = true

        # controls how soon a shake is detected
        # lower values mean sooner
        threshold = 6.0

        # magnification level immediately after shake start
        base = 4.0
        # magnification increase per second when continuing to shake
        speed = 4.0
        # how much the speed is influenced by the current shake intensitiy
        influence = 0.0

        # maximal magnification the cursor can reach
        # values below 1 disable the limit (e.g. 0)
        limit = 0.0

        # time in millseconds the cursor will stay magnified after a shake has ended
        timeout = 2000

        # show cursor behaviour `tilt`, `rotate`, etc. while shaking
        effects = rotate

        # enable ipc events for shake
        # see the `ipc` section below
        ipc = true
    }

    # use hyprcursor to get a higher resolution texture when the cursor is magnified
    # see the `hyprcursor` section below
    hyprcursor {

        # use nearest-neighbour (pixelated) scaling when magnifing beyond texture size
        # this will also have effect without hyprcursor support being enabled
        # 0 / false - never use pixelated scaling
        # 1 / true  - use pixelated when no highres image
        # 2         - always use pixleated scaling
        nearest = true

        # enable dedicated hyprcursor support
            enabled = true

        # resolution in pixels to load the magnified shapes at
        # be warned that loading a very high-resolution image will take a long time and might impact memory consumption
        # -1 means we use [normal cursor size] * [shake:base option]
            resolution = -1

            # shape to use when clientside cursors are being magnified
            # see the shape-name property of shape rules for possible names
            # specifying clientside will use the actual shape, but will be pixelated
            fallback = clientside
        }
    }
}          
```

Indeed it does work like this. I will do as you asked, i just need some time and will get back to you as soon as i figure out which one is breaking it.

---

So, here's the culprit:
ControllerHotPlug = true

By setting that to true, at least on my AllyX makes the game crash on startup after some 2-3 seconds as described.
Also, this setting:

title: [Bug]: CD Switcher causing consistent crashes when transitioning to the next song (not skip).
body:
### Tweaks version

v0.4.1 with the loading time fix that you posted in the other issue thread

### Describe your issue here (please attach the OutRun2006Tweaks.log file with your report, you can drag+drop it into the text area)

I added some songs to the switcher, but I've been getting consistent crashes. It appears that if I let it transition to the next song rather than skipping, it causes a crash.  I tested this multiple times, and it's consistent.

This does not seem to occur with the base game ogg files. If I had to guess, it's because normally the ogg files are set to loop by the game, but since that doesn't exist for the FLACs (or oggs that you add that don't replace any of the base filenames, since they don't have anything that tells them to loop), it doesn't know what to do when it reaches the end of the song and crashes.

Does the CD Switcher actually have a function to transition to the next song, or does it just play it? As a stopgap measure, perhaps a function that automatically skips the song when it reaches the last second could be implemented until this is hopefully fixes. Or to imitate the original game, and tell any CD Switcher songs to loop endlessly?

I'm surprised that no one else seems to have brought this up before. I guess everyone else is either lucky, not using the CDS, or has just been skipping songs manually the entire time.
[OutRun2006Tweaks.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16232713/OutRun2006Tweaks.log)

[esp32 wifi relay project maybe useful](https://github.com/dchristl/esp32_nat_router_extended)'}, {'user': 'francescopace', 'created_at': '2025-12-31T15:11:43Z', 'body': "Thanks for the suggestion @gasment, there are no wrong or immature question here, but I'd like to understand your use case better. 1. **Why do you need a separate AP per room?** ESPectre works fine with a standard WiFi router shared across multiple rooms. Each ESPectre device generates its own traffic (100 pps) to the router and detects motion independently. 2. **Is it a coverage issue?** If your main router doesn't reach all rooms, a simple WiFi repeater or mesh system would be simpler than an ESP32 AP. You typically only need one repeater per floor, not per room. 3. **Home Assistant connectivity?** If an ESP32 acts as a dedicated AP with its own network (e.g., 192.168.4.x), the ESPectre devices connected to it would be **isolated from your main network** and unable to communicate with Home Assistant. ``` ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Home Assistant │ │ ESP32-AP │ │ 192.168.1.x │ ❌ ISOLATED │ 192.168.4.1 │ │ Main Network │ │ Separate Net │ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ │ ┌──────┴──────┐ │ ESPectre │ │ 192.168.4.x │ │ Can't reach │ │ Home Assist │ └─────────────┘ ``` For problem number 3 there are two possible workarounds to explore: 1. **AP+STA mode**: The ESP32-AP connects to your main network (STA) while also running its own AP. This works but adds complexity - the ESP32-AP would need to act as a bridge or NAT, which has limitations (few clients, added latency). 2. **Aggregator pattern**: ESPectre devices send their motion state to the ESP32-AP via a custom protocol, and the ESP32-AP reports aggregated data to Home Assistant. This requires significant new code. The `threshold_number` entity in Home Assistant allows you to adjust that value **at runtime** without reflashing. When you change it from HA, the new value is saved to NVS (persistent memory) and becomes the active threshold. So: - YAML `segmentation_threshold: 1.0` → initial value at first boot - HA `threshold_number` → live adjustment, saved persistently Generally speaking, for WiFi motion detection with CSI, positions in corners opposite to the AP are often optimal because of: - Maximum multipath: The signal from the AP reaches the corner after bouncing off multiple walls, creating many different paths - More paths to disturb: When you move in the room, you interrupt/modify many of these ray paths simultaneously → stronger CSI variations - Favorable geometry: From the opposite corner, movement in the center of the room intersects virtually all the main radio paths - Better coverage: The corner "sees" (in radio terms) the entire room, not just a portion If you want to go deep, I suggest you this [paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2412.13208) covering all of this aspects: --- > when I plug the esp32 power (I squat down nearby esp32 and even hold my breathe） About calibration @gasment: No need to squat down and hold your breath, I don't want any fainting incidents on my conscience! 😄 Just keep the room reasonably still (no people walking around). title: Can't build on MacOS after commit a667670
body:
Hello,

I don't know much about C and compilers, so, please correct me if I'm wrong. But apparently, I haven't been able to build pogocache on my Macbook because of this line:

https://github.com/tidwall/pogocache/blob/main/src/sys.c#L250

When running "make", it threw me this error:

```
cd src && /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/make all
cc -Wall -Wextra -Werror -g -O3 -flto=auto    -c -o sys.o sys.c
sys.c:250:5: error: 'TARGET_OS_MAC' is not defined, evaluates to 0 [-Werror,-Wundef-prefix=TARGET_OS_]
  250 | #if TARGET_OS_MAC || TARGET_OS_IOS
      |     ^
sys.c:250:22: error: 'TARGET_OS_IOS' is not defined, evaluates to 0 [-Werror,-Wundef-prefix=TARGET_OS_]
  250 | #if TARGET_OS_MAC || TARGET_OS_IOS
      |                      ^
2 errors generated.
make[1]: *** [sys.o] Error 1

It looks like this line was introduced by the commit a667670, so I've tried to compile pogocache using a preview commit (84511ac) and it compiled just fine.

So I guess it's a regression, unfortunately.

title: [Bug] Non cacheline aligned arena allocations
author: jlombera
comments:
[{'user': 'nicbarker', 'created_at': '2025-06-16T08:58:40Z', 'body': "Hello 👋
Ah yes you're absolutely right, AFAIK `malloc` and friends will return 8 byte aligned on modern systems so at least that case is covered, but it makes sense for us to consider a misaligned initial provided `memory` pointer as part of both the min memory size and setting the initial `nextAllocation` offset, rather than leaving it as zero.
Should be a quick and easy fix, I will put it in tomorrow 👍 "}, {'user': 'jlombera', 'created_at': '2025-06-16T19:26:22Z', 'body': "> AFAIK `malloc` and friends will return 8 byte aligned on modern systems so at least that case is covered, but it makes sense for us to consider a misaligned initial provided `memory` pointer [...]

The code tries to align to cacheline, i.e. 64 bytes instead of 8.  So even when memory comes from `malloc(3)` it's not guarantee it'll be cacheline aligned.


> [...] and setting the initial nextAllocation offset, rather than leaving it as zero.

Just setting `nextAllocation` initially won't help.  Next time the offset is computed solely based on the value of `nextAllocation` (as in `(1)` above), it'll result in a misaligned address (because `memory` is still misaligned).

You have to either:
a) Adjust `memory` so that it's aligned.  Afterwards it will be safe to compute the offset based only on the value of `nextAllocation`.  Or

b) Take into account both `nextAllocation` and `memory` alignment when an offset is computed.  E.g. (I haven't double checked the correctness of the computation):
```c
offset = nextAllocation + (64 - ((memory + nextAllocation) % 64));

return (memory + offset);
```"}, {'user': 'nicbarker', 'created_at': '2025-06-17T00:53:37Z', 'body': "Yes you're right! I've aligned the base `memory` pointer to 64 here:
https://github.com/nicbarker/clay/commit/b9e27178c0aee15ff77351335b2643eca2423502
Let me know what you think!"}, {'user': 'jlombera', 'created_at': '2025-06-17T02:25:50Z', 'body': "It looks good.  I would have done that `memory` adjustment when the arena is created, though (e.g. in `Clay_CreateArenaWithCapacityAndMemory()`), but that's me 😃 "}, {'user': 'nicbarker', 'created_at': '2025-06-17T03:03:16Z', 'body': "@jlombera while that would normally be very sensible, I've seen people constructing the arena struct by hand and passing it in rather than calling `CreateArenaWithCapacityAndMemory`, so I thought I might try to catch those cases as well 🙂"}, {'user': 'jlombera', 'created_at': '2025-06-17T03:57:27Z', 'body': 'I see, that makes sense.  Personally, I would be less lenient: "It's the user's problem if they don't use the API as intended" 😉.

But looking into the examples, it seems the only use the user has of `Clay_Arena` is to pass it to `Clay_Initialize()`.  So I was wondering, why not make the arena an internal definition instead?  `Clay_Initialize()` might instead receive just the pointer to the memory and length.  The proper arena creation and initialization (e.g. address alignment) would be done internally.  I see some benefits doing this:
- Makes the API a little simpler, with one less concept the user has to think about.
- You ensure the arena is properly initialized internally, without user intervention.
- You don't expose the arena, removing the chances of user messing with it (even if by mistake).
- The API feels less "verbose".  To me, as a user, having to construct an API object, just to pass it to another API function and never touch it again always evokes the reaction: "why don't you construct it yourself internally? why do I have to litter my code with these repetitive definitions that have no use from my side?" (The exception to this is when memory allocation is required.  I want to have control of memory allocation.  I rather the API ask me to construct the object myself than it allocating memory from the heap (`malloc(3)`) internally.  I _do_ like that Clay asks for the memory to be used internally)'}, {'user': 'nicbarker', 'created_at': '2025-06-17T23:27:09Z', 'body': 'I'd say I agree with most of the points there, the API grew organically and it feels like a little bit of ceremony now (4 functions or something just to get things "initialized") so it could definitely be time for a cleanup 🙂'}]
satisfaction_conditions: A solution that ensures all arena allocations are properly aligned to cacheline boundaries (64 bytes) regardless of the initial memory pointer alignment
The alignment correction must account for the relationship between the base memory pointer and allocation offsets, not just one or the other
The solution must handle cases where users provide their own memory pointer to the arena, including potentially misaligned pointers

title: CAS is not working (or I'm doing something wrong)
body:
I'm trying to figure out how to avoid race conditions when working with the same key in multiple threads (the end goal is to implement query on top of pogocache). I've read about CAS in Memcached, so I'm trying to use it. Simplest example that I came up with: 1) two threads 2) each thread reads value with **gets**; 3) each tries to update value with **cas**; 4) if update fails - wait some time and try to read and update again.

```python
import memcache 
import threading
import time

SERVER_URL = 'pogocache:9401'
#SERVER_URL = 'memcached:11211'

def worker(worker_id):
    mc = memcache.Client([SERVER_URL], debug=1, cache_cas=True)

    def increment():
        value = mc.gets('counter')
        print(f"Worker {worker_id} gets: {value=}")
        value = int(value) + 1
        cas_result = mc.cas('counter', str(value))
        print(f"Worker {worker_id} cas: {cas_result=}")
        return cas_result
    
    if increment() is False:
        time.sleep(0.1)
        increment()


if __name__ =="__main__":
    mc = memcache.Client([SERVER_URL], debug=1, cache_cas=True)
    mc.delete('counter')
    mc.add('counter', '0')

    t1 = threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(1,))
    t2 = threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(2,))

    t1.start()
    t2.start()

    t1.join()
    t2.join()

    print(mc.get('counter'))
```

**What I expect**:
In the end counter is equal to 2 every time
**What actually happens**
Half of the time counter is equal to 1 (race condition)

**Logs**
* Pogocache (pid: 1, arch: linux/x86_64, version: 1.0.1-2-g06bea1f, git: 06bea1f)
* Memory (system: 15.3G, max: 80%/12.3G, evict: yes)
* Features (verbosity: normal, sixpack: yes, **cas: yes**, persist: none, uring: no)
* Network (port: 9401, unixsocket: none, backlog: 1024, reuseport: no, maxconns: 1024)
* Socket (tcpnodelay: yes, keepalive: yes, quickack: no)
* Threads (threads: 12, queuesize: 128)
* Shards (shards: 4096, loadfactor: 75%)
* Security (auth: disabled, tlsport: none)
* Network listener established
* Ready to accept connections

I also tried the same code with Memcached, and it works as expected.

title: Bug at SUBGHZ bruteforce
body: I discovered a potential issue with the bruteforce command in SUBGHZ mode. After running bruteforce and stopping it with the Enter key, the transmitter remains active across the entire band, as shown in the attached screenshot. The only way to stop the transmission is to power-cycle the board. Neither a system reboot nor pressing the onboard RST button resolves the problem. Upon reviewing Bruce firmware (from which SUBGHZ mode was adapted), I noticed a call to the deinitRfModule() function after stopping bruteforce. This function sets the CS pin to HIGH and the GDO0 pin to LOW. It seems this step might be missing in the ESP32-Bus-Pirate implementation of SUBGHZ bruteforce, which could explain the persistent transmission.

title: Potential Timing Oracle in Basic Auth
body:
Very cool project! I love the structure of the source and the whole vibe of it.

I noticed a potential security bug, likely low risk [2]:

https://github.com/ashtonjamesd/lavandula/blob/3333c76da6fdc14e81e1c6cd830bb079550ff5bf/src/auth.c#L61

Depending on the implementation [1], `strcmp()` might (not not!) compare one byte at a time, creating a very small but statistically detectable difference in request handling time between having ex. zero correct password bytes, and one first correct password byte. Over many requests, one can then use this timing difference to guess the password one/a few bytes at a time.

Still, I've seen papers demonstrate timing attacks on nanosecond delays, and "implementation dependent security risk" makes me uneasy. What I would suggest is just hashing both sides of the strcmp() beforehand, with some kind of cryptographic hash function. 

Hope this is helpful! And very cool project!!

[1] https://www.sjoerdlangkemper.nl/2024/05/29/string-comparison-timing-attacks/

[2] I looked for a security / disclosure policy, but couldn't find any. I decided the transparency about memory issues was a sufficient "don't actually use this yet" marker to just make a bug report for this kind of low risk thing. Please let me know if you disagree.

title: docs: Some suggestions to "On-Disk Storage"
body:
In https://lite3.io/design_and_limitations.html#autotoc_md41 some parts may benefit from some detai:

> This is dangerous, because if the system crashes while syncing data to disk, the structure can end up in a corrupt intermediate state. The most reliable atomic pattern is to write your new data to a temporary file, flush and sync it to disk, then use the `rename()` syscall to replace the target file. On Linux, `rename()` is atomic at the filesystem level.

If you want durability (which you do seem to want given that you talk about "sync it to disk"), you need to both `fsync` file and `fsync` the parent directory, otherwise your `fsync`ed inode will be somewhere on the disk but your `rename()` may not have been durably persisted.

> ### `mmap()`
>
> Write-maps do not have built-in atomicity. Even when calling `fsync()`

Should that be `msync()`?

> Even when calling `fsync()` manually, you rely on the OS to sync changes to disk.

Not sure I understand. You rely on the OS implementing your `*sync()` operation of course, and it makes sense to rely on it (just as much as `fsync` for files).

Maybe the sentence should be

> Write-maps do not have built-in atomicity. Even when calling `msync()`, a crash during it could leave your data ..."
author: nh2
comments:
[{'user': 'eliasdejong', 'created_at': '2025-12-20T19:42:57Z', 'body': 'Atomically changing the contents of a file on Linux indeed turns out to require more steps than I naively assumed. I now changed the text to the following:
> > direct file I/O
> 
> This is dangerous, because if the system crashes while syncing data to disk, the structure can end up in a corrupt intermediate state. To atomically update the contents of a file on Linux, a very specific sequence of steps is required. If not followed exactly, data could be at risk during a crash or power-out event.
> 
> The steps are as follows:
> 1. create a new temporary file (on the same file system!)
> 2. write data to the temporary file
> 3. fsync() the temporary file
> 4. rename the temporary file to the appropriate name (using the `rename()` syscall)
> 5. fsync() the containing directory
> 
> For more information, see: [https://lwn.net/Articles/457667](https://lwn.net/Articles/457667)

Then to address your other comment:

> Maybe the sentence should be
>> Write-maps do not have built-in atomicity. Even when calling msync(), a crash during it could leave your data ..."

Yes, thank you for pointing that out. This has now also been updated in the docs page.'}]
satisfaction_conditions: Documentation must accurately describe the complete sequence of operations required for atomic file updates on Linux, including both file and directory synchronization
Documentation must use the correct system call terminology when discussing memory-mapped file synchronization
Documentation must clarify the relationship between synchronization operations and crash safety for memory-mapped files
Documentation must provide authoritative external references for complex durability guarantees

title: [Bug] Brew stops without reaching the target weight
body:
### Brief summary of the bug

Machine stops brewing when reached time limit for a given phase even when a target weight is specified to stop at.

### Describe the issue in greater detail

With version 1.6.0 the brew stops when reaching the time limit of given phase without reaching the weight target.


I am using a Bookoo scale.

### Are you able to reproduce the issue?

Yes

### Steps to reproduce

1. power on
2. power on scale (wait for connection)
3. set brew type to go by weight
4. select a brew profile with "stop when" defined for weight reached
5. zero the scale
6. start brew

### Expected behavior

Expected would be to have the brew continue even after the set time is over if needed and only stop when given weight is reached.

### Has this function/fetaure worked before with your GaggiMate?

Yes

### Relevant logs or error messages

```shell

```

### Firmware version

both on 1.6.0

### What machine are you experiencing this issue on?

_No response_

### Additional context

I thought the new software on the controller would be the issue so I downgraded that to 1.5.0 and kept the screen at 1.6.0 version, but the issue persisted. Only went away after downgrading both to 1.5.0.

"}, {'user': 'AncientJames', 'created_at': '2025-06-09T22:58:45Z', 'body': "The code compensates for the distance the LEDs travel, to maintain uniform brightness / density. The bigger problem is that when the panel is edge on to the viewer, the brightness drops off. This is an inescapable consequence of using panels with the LEDs all in one plane - each pixel is a nice bright circle when face on, but becomes thinner and thinner at glancing angles until it's just an infinitessimal line. This manifests itself as a dark wedge going through the centre of the volume.

Putting the two panels at different offsets from the axis helps reduce this effect. One panel goes right through the axis, which enables it to addres columns right in the centre, at the cost of extremely glancing angles along the line to the viewer. The other panel is further out where it can't address the centre or the region behind the axis, but has better viewing angles in the front and centre region where it matters most.

Further from the axis, the two panels are largely the same and just give a doubling of the frame rate. In the middle, they complement each other and cover up some of each other's drawbacks.

You can make it out in the water in this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ILNbnWneTIg - there's a dark triangular region that extends out from the centre to the back of the display. If it only had a single panel on the axis, that same feature would extend all the way to the front as well. The second, offset, panel is what fills it in. You can see that the dark triangle in front of the axis cuts off against a well lit circle, which is as close in as the second panel comes. You can also see that the radial lines overlap each other in a cross hatch pattern at the front - this is the two panels passing through that region at different angles due to their offset.

"}]

author: BlenderRender3D
comments:
[{'user': 'BlenderRender3D', 'created_at': '2025-05-11T15:47:17Z', 'body': 'I looked into it a bit more. I reverted the files gadget_rotovox.h and gadget_vortex.h and compiled the project without my changes. I thought, if I do not need to change my pin assignment for https://github.com/hzeller/rpi-rgb-led-matrix then I probably need to use the pins as they are assigned in this project. And when I make changes then I get a lot of warnings when compiling. If I run vortex then it is showing output on the commandline as expected. But the screens stay black. Then I also run tesseract but the screens stay black. I had some times when there were some stripes on the screen, but after disabling a sound chip which the other project complained about I did not have the stripes anymore.'}, {'user': 'AncientJames', 'created_at': '2025-05-11T22:32:53Z', 'body': "The documentation you have there is showing a mapping based on the numbering of the pins on the Pi's header, but the multivox code is using the internal GPIO numbers. If you look at https://pinout.xyz, you'll see how the pin numbers map to GPIO numbers.

Translating that document to show the gpio numbers, and renaming the signals to match the way they're named in the code, you end up with this:


```
-              |    -
(RGB_2_G1)  2  |     -
(RGB_2_B1)  3  |     GND
RGB_STROBE  4  |  14 (RGB_2_R1)
-              |  15 ROW_E
RGB_CLOCK  17  |  18 RGB_BLANK
RGB_0_G1   27  |     -
ROW_A      22  |  23 ROW_B
-              |  24 ROW_C
RGB_0_B2   10  |     -
RGB_0_G2    9  |  25 ROW_D
RGB_0_R1   11  |   8 RGB_0_R2
-              |   7 RGB_0_B1
-              |     -
RGB_1_G1    5  |     -
RGB_1_B1    6  |  12 RGB_1_R1
RGB_1_G2   13  |     -
RGB_1_R2   19  |  16 (RGB_2_G2)
(RGB_2_R2) 26  |  20 RGB_1_B2
-              |  21 (RGB_2_B2)
```

`BLANK` is `OE`, `STROBE` is `LAT`, and `CLOCK` is `CLK`.

`ROW_A`, `ROW_B`,  `ROW_C`, `ROW_D`,  `ROW_E` are the `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, `E` pins on the HUB75E connector. In the original HUB75 interface these were simply the bits specifying the row currently being addressed, with `A` the LSB and `E` MSB. The rotovox gadget uses them this way because that's the style of panel it uses. As LED panels have moved to higher densities, the manufacturers have started to use different schemes for addressing each row. They still use the ABCDE naming on the connector, but those pins now carry a different signal, generally poorly documented and up to the user to decipher.

The panels used in the vortex gadget use A, B and C to carry signals shifting in the address a bit at a time. In the code I've named them `ADDR_CLK`, `ADDR_DAT`, and `ADDR__EN` - it was trial and error to discover which line took which signal.

If you have an original style panel, you define the `ROW_?` pins and leave the `ADDR_*` pins undefined. The driver code chooses what to compile based on which set is defined. (`ADDR__EN_MASK` appears in both code paths, so it needs to be defined as 0 if it's not used).

Putting all that together, the gadget mapping for ABCDE panels connected to your interface board would be:

```
#define RGB_0_R1 11
#define RGB_0_G1 27
#define RGB_0_B1 7
#define RGB_0_R2 8
#define RGB_0_G2 9
#define RGB_0_B2 10

#define RGB_1_R1 12
#define RGB_1_G1 5
#define RGB_1_B1 6
#define RGB_1_R2 19
#define RGB_1_G2 13
#define RGB_1_B2 20

#define ROW_A 22
#define ROW_B 23
#define ROW_C 24
#define ROW_D 25
#define ROW_E 15
#define ADDR__EN_MASK (0)

#define RGB_BLANK 18
#define RGB_CLOCK 17
#define RGB_STROBE 4
#define RGB_BLANK_MASK (1<<RGB_BLANK)
#define RGB_CLOCK_MASK (1<<RGB_CLOCK)
#define RGB_STROBE_MASK (1<<RGB_STROBE)
```

title: Question: SSL probe attachment failure for Node.js binary
body:
The logs show repeated warnings indicating a failure to attach SSL probes to /usr/bin/node, along with event drops due to a full channel.

```
time="2025-10-09T11:16:44Z" level=warning msg="Failed to process library event" error="failed to attach SSL probes to /usr/bin/node (inode 35280): failed to attach SSL_read entry uprobe: symbol SSL_read: not found" path=/usr/bin/node
time="2025-10-09T11:16:44Z" level=warning msg="Event channel full, dropping event"
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1.	Run the binary with Node.js processes present on the system.
2.	Observe logs around startup or library load events.


## Environment
	•	Binary: /usr/bin/node
	•	OS: kernel(6.14.0-1013-aws) ubuntu (24.04) arch (x86_64)
	•	Architecture: amd64/arm64


Should we attempt to attach SSL probes to Node.js binaries by default, or skip them when the relevant OpenSSL symbols (like SSL_read) are not found? 

Just want to clarify the design intent here. Thanks!

comments:
[{'user': 'alex-ilgayev', 'created_at': '2025-10-10T09:34:41Z', 'body': "@abhisheksoam, thank you for providing the information.

To properly debug this, can you provide the following:
- Node version through `node --version`
- How did you install Node in your system? Were it `apt install` `apk add`, `nvm`, etc.

Regarding your questions, from my understanding, Node executables should have the OpenSSL symbols statically linked, so the `node` executable should have these symbols. If you are using `node` in a way that is working differently (in some way dynamically linking `libssl`) I would love to test that, and accordingly adapt the code. That's why I'm interested in reproducing that.

Regarding `Event channel full, dropping event`, can you elaborate a bit on the environment? Were you doing heavy lifting? processes that are heavily consuming the filesystem?
We can solve that easily by increasing the channel size, but I want to check first what the scenarios are, because I didn't encounter it in my tests.

Thanks!

> Node version through node --version

- Node version: v20.18.1

> Regarding “Event channel full, dropping event,” can you elaborate a bit on the environment? Were you doing heavy lifting or running processes that heavily use the filesystem?


No heavy load, it seems the issue occurs while attaching probes.

```
main.go:107
// Process library events

libManager := ebpf.NewLibraryManager(loader, mountNS)
defer libManager.Close()

-> This sets `retryOnError` to true by default, which causes the second condition to fail.
-> As a result, it keeps retrying to attach the SSL probe.

library_manager.go:65
    // Check if previously failed and retryOnError is disabled
    if err, ok := lm.failedLibs[inode]; ok && !lm.retryOnError {
        logrus.WithFields(logrus.Fields{

    }
```

So, it seems that because retryOnError is set to true by default, the condition never passes, causing continuous retries while attempting to attach the SSL probe. Does it include the `Event channel full, dropping event` issue as well? Like it stopped appearing?'}, {'user': 'abhisheksoam', 'created_at': '2025-10-10T10:22:27Z', 'body': 'Yes, that also resolved the `Event channel full, dropping event issue.`

Code snippet:
```
main.go:120

libManager := ebpf.NewLibraryManagerWithRetry(loader, mountNS, false)
defer libManager.Close()
``` '}, {'user': 'alex-ilgayev', 'created_at': '2025-10-11T18:51:09Z', 'body': "@abhisheksoam 
I implemented a partial fix here: #65 
Can you run again your setup?

You will still see a warning (I will eventually fix it), but it shouldn't retry it, and hopefully, the channel shouldn't be full."}, {'user': 'abhisheksoam', 'created_at': '2025-10-13T03:58:08Z', 'body': "> [@abhisheksoam](https://github.com/abhisheksoam) I implemented a partial fix here: [#65](https://github.com/alex-ilgayev/MCPSpy/pull/65) Can you run again your setup?
> 
> You will still see a warning (I will eventually fix it), but it shouldn't retry it, and hopefully, the channel shouldn't be full.

Yes, this resolves the issue partially. How do you plan to address it in the future? I mean, in terms of design choices."}, {'user': 'alex-ilgayev', 'created_at': '2025-10-14T12:38:09Z', 'body': "> > [@abhisheksoam](https://github.com/abhisheksoam) I implemented a partial fix here: [#65](https://github.com/alex-ilgayev/MCPSpy/pull/65) Can you run again your setup?
> > You will still see a warning (I will eventually fix it), but it shouldn't retry it, and hopefully, the channel shouldn't be full.
> 
> Yes, this resolves the issue partially. How do you plan to address it in the future? I mean, in terms of design choices.

@abhisheksoam This warning is actually legitimate and not hurting the functionality. Esthetically speaking, we could put that under debug, because it revolves around legitimate usage. The reason it's in a warning is that there could be some behavior that could hurt the program.

A little bit of background on why that happened in the first place - some `node` distribution linking`libssl` statically, means the `SSL_read` and `SSL_write` methods are within the `node` executable, and some are linking it dynamically, means we should hook into `libssl.*`.
We are trying to seek every executable named `node` before we know how it is linking to `libssl`, so we may fail. In your case (which I managed to reproduce), even though it is failing to hook to `node`, it is successfully hooking into the linked `libssl`, thus the program functionality is unhurt.

So I'm not really concerned about this behavior, except for some warning that may mislead/deter."}, {'user': 'abhisheksoam', 'created_at': '2025-10-14T14:41:55Z', 'body': 'Got it, that makes sense. Thanks for the detailed explanation!
 I agree, since it’s not impacting functionality and stems from how Node links `libssl` differently across builds, it’s reasonable to downgrade this to a debug log. The warning might indeed cause unnecessary concern otherwise.'}, {'user': 'alex-ilgayev', 'created_at': '2025-10-24T07:04:14Z', 'body': 'Thanks for the feedback, closing as it is solved'}]

title: Font size rounding seems wrong for alpha glyphs
body:
When calling `skb_render_cache_get_glyph_quad` with `SKB_RENDER_ALPHA_MASK` with the default image config, the font size rounding and scale calculation seems incorrect (or I'm misunderstanding the intent).

This line:
```
	const float rounded_font_size = skb_ceilf(font_size * pixel_scale / img_config->rounding) * img_config->rounding;
```

If you pass in `48.0f` for `font_size`, and `1.0f` for `pixel_scale`, the calculated `rounded_font_size` will be 49.0f, which then results in a `render_scale` later in the function of `48.0 / 49.0` or `.979`.

I'm guessing the intent of the default rounding value for alpha glyphs is to not adjust the font size at all and leave the scale at 1.0?

      - '/var/mounts/beszel/beszel_data:/beszel_data'
  beszel-agent:
    image: 'henrygd/beszel-agent:latest'
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    environment:
      - 'DOCKER_HOST=tcp://socket-proxy:2375'
      - PORT=45876
      - >-
        KEY=ssh-ed25519
        AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIKN1E5TF2lzh4Otb2sfyMY0b7jVFRD26UlZ4UhB5owN9
  socket-proxy:
    image: 'lscr.io/linuxserver/socket-proxy:latest'
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - CONTAINERS=1
    volumes:
      - '/var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro'
    read_only: true
    tmpfs:
      - /run
```

I've made a few vain attempts at making this work, mostly by increasing permissions (`POST=1`, `ALLOW_RESTARTS=1`, `ALLOW_RESTARTS=1`, `ALLOW_START=1`, `ALLOW_STOP=1`) eventually abandoning brute-force and actually reading the code of both projects.

Unfortunately, reading the pertinent parts ([ref](https://github.com/henrygd/beszel/blob/main/beszel/internal/agent/docker.go), [ref](https://github.com/Tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy/blob/master/haproxy.cfg)) doesn't really tell me why this would break. It seems like it should just work!

Does anyone else have any hints on why container stats would be missing in such a simple setup?

The solution is to expose the the proxy on localhost (this does not allow external connections), then use localhost to connect from the agent.

title: `RequestExtra.CloseSSEStream` function field breaks JSON serialization of request types
body:
**Describe the bug**
The `CloseSSEStream` field added to the `RequestExtra` is a function type, which causes `json.Marshal` to fail on any `ServerRequest`-derived type. This breaks common use cases like logging, debugging output, or persisting protocol requests.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Use `json.Marshal` on any of the `ServerRequest` types

**Expected behavior**
I should be able to marshal any request type to JSON

**Additional context**
I'd be happy to open a fix to this issue if appropriate. I believe all is needed is to add a `json:"-"` tag.
author: Cali0707
comments:
[{'user': 'findleyr', 'created_at': '2026-01-02T18:09:50Z', 'body': "I don't think it's intended that the Request types be JSON serializable. They're an encapsulation of the incoming request context, including the session and RequestExtra. If they were serializable before, it's a coincidence: certainly we made no guarantees that the Session be serializable, and it's an exported field.

Notably, the request is NOT the protocol request.

I think a better solution for your use-case would be to actually store the raw protocol request (a `jsonrpc.Request`). on the `mcp.Request` type."}, {'user': 'Cali0707', 'created_at': '2026-01-02T20:17:58Z', 'body': 'Ah okay that was a misunderstanding on my end then.'}]
satisfaction_conditions: Clarification of the intended design and serialization capabilities of the Request types
Guidance on the appropriate alternative approach for persisting or logging request data
Explanation of the distinction between protocol requests and the Request wrapper types

title: main() function logic not executed, but top-level invocation not allowed — trapped in execution dead zone
body:
## Summary

There's a behavior inconsistency when wrapping shell scripts for Bunster compilation:

1. If I place all logic inside a `main()` function but do **not** call it, the compiled binary executes nothing.
2. If I attempt to call `main` at the top level (i.e. outside of any function), the compiler fails with the error:


## Example

Input script:

```sh
#! /bin/sh

main() {
    echo "success replace!" 
    echo "Current directory: $(pwd)"
    echo "List hidden files:" 
    ls -al ~/.config 
    echo "Print \$PATH variable:" 
    echo "$PATH" > 1.log 
    echo "Escaped quotes: He said, \"Hello world!\""
}

main
```
user@c0401f469bb7:~$ bunster build /tmp/a_wrap.sh -o ./test   
Error:  main.sh(0:0): semantic error: only functions can exist in global scope.

## Expected Behavior
Either Bunster should automatically invoke main() as an entry point if present;

Or it should allow top-level function calls for execution purposes;

Alternatively, support a documented convention (e.g. __bunster_run()) that the compiler will automatically invoke.

## Environment
Bunster version: v0.13.0

Go version: go 1.23.8 linux/amd64

OS: Linux container (Debian)

## Suggestions
Add documentation on how to correctly define an entry point.

Consider relaxing global scope restrictions for main() invocation.

Or provide a flag/config to designate the function to invoke at runtime.

Thanks for the great project—this tool has tremendous potential if this blocker gets addressed!

Hello, a blind user here. :)

## Reproduction steps

1. Open the app on its main screen.
2. Turn on Talkback by long pressing the up and down volume keys.
3. use left / right swipes to move around the screen.

## Expected behavior

After the labels denoting the selected model and language, the screenreader should read the spinners with their selected values. Also, on the TextView with the result text, it should read the content of the component.

## Actual behavior

The screenreader can find the spinners as well as the TextView, but only reads their description, not their value.

## Explanation

The reason for this bug is the usage of the contentDescription attribute in the activity layout file. contentDescription is typically used on static widgets, where the screenreader has no way of determining how to meaningfully report the widget to the user. For example, the record button and the other buttons on the screen are a perfect use-case for this attribute, because they're just icon buttons, and the screenreader is unable to communicate their purpose represented by the embedded images.

However, for components carying a dynamic value, like the spinners and the result TextView, this value is what screenreaders need to report to the user, so the contentDescription is not necessary. In fact, it is actually counterproductive, since it overrides the component dynamic value, which the user needs to access. In these scenarios, VI users can determine the purpose of the component by its adjacent label, which is accessible for the screenreaders.

## Solution

Removing the contentDescription attribute from the spinners and the result TextView makes thing work really nicely on my phone. :)

I could open a PR, but it's really just 3 line change.

Thanks for the great job!

title: MCP server stdio mode corrupted by stdout log messages
body:
## Bug Description

The MCP server startup code in `src/cli/simple-commands/mcp.js` outputs log messages to **stdout** during stdio mode initialization, which corrupts the JSON-RPC protocol stream and causes errors in MCP clients.

## Root Cause

When running `npx claude-flow mcp start` (which defaults to stdio mode), the code outputs startup messages to stdout using `printSuccess()`:

```javascript
printSuccess('Starting Claude Flow MCP server in stdio mode...');
```

This outputs to **stdout**:
```
✅ Starting Claude Flow MCP server in stdio mode...
```

In MCP's stdio mode, **stdout must be reserved exclusively for JSON-RPC protocol messages**. Any other output corrupts the protocol stream.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run: `npx claude-flow mcp start`
2. Observe MCP client errors due to corrupted JSON-RPC stream
3. Check stdout output - startup messages appear on stdout instead of being silent

## Expected Behavior

- The wrapper function in `simple-commands/mcp.js` should be **completely silent**
- It only spawns the real MCP server with `stdio: 'inherit'`
- The actual MCP server (`src/mcp/mcp-server.js`) already handles proper logging to stderr
- Wrapper messages are redundant and harmful

## Actual Behavior

- Wrapper outputs unnecessary startup messages to stdout
- This corrupts the JSON-RPC protocol stream
- MCP clients cannot parse the output

## Impact

- MCP server cannot be used in stdio mode with standard MCP clients
- Affects all users trying to use claude-flow as an MCP server
- Bug has existed since July 8, 2025 (commit 29800626c, PR #167)

## Affected Code

`src/cli/simple-commands/mcp.js` lines 51-97:
- Line 53: `printSuccess('Starting Claude Flow MCP server in stdio mode...')` 
- Lines 56-61: Auto-orchestrator status messages
- Lines 88-91: Exit handler messages
- Lines 105-112: Fallback error messages

All of these should be **removed** for stdio mode.

## Solution

The wrapper function should be **completely silent** in stdio mode:

```javascript
if (stdio) {
  // Start MCP server in stdio mode (like ruv-swarm)
  // The actual MCP server will handle all logging to stderr
  try {
    // ... spawn server with stdio: 'inherit' ...
    
    serverProcess.on('exit', (code) => {
      // Silent exit - server handles its own logging
      if (code !== 0) {
        process.exit(code);
      }
    });
    
    await new Promise(() => {}); // Never resolves, keeps server running
  } catch (error) {
    // Silent fail - the spawned server will handle error logging
    process.exit(1);
  }
}
```

## Why Remove Instead of Stderr?

The wrapper just spawns the real server with `stdio: 'inherit'`, which means:
1. The real MCP server (`src/mcp/mcp-server.js`) already logs properly to stderr
2. Wrapper messages are redundant
3. Even stderr messages from the wrapper add noise
4. Clean separation: wrapper is silent, server handles all I/O

## Git History

Introduced in:
- Commit: 29800626c9a3688ab8a5c0b1364b2dbedbacd7b1
- Date: July 8, 2025
- PR: #167 "feat: implement critical hook safety system & resolve all init issues"
- Author: rUv

Persisted through:
- v2.0.0-alpha.59 (6207ea53)
- v2.0.0-alpha.62 (fd295cda)  
- v2.5.0-alpha.131 (85a8988c)

## References

- MCP Protocol Specification: stdio transport requires clean stdout
- Real MCP server implementation: `src/mcp/mcp-server.js` (properly uses stderr)

title: Use ISO 639 Codes for Languages
body:
There is an [ISO standard](https://www.iso.org/iso-639-language-code) for [language codes](https://www.loc.gov/standards/iso639-2/php/code_list.php) that is much more common than the arbitrary language codes you've made up.

For differentiating by country, it is usually followed by an underscore `_` or a dash `-`, and the [ISO 3166](https://www.iso.org/iso-3166-country-codes.html) [country code](https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/#search).

English from the USA = `en_US`, English from the UK = `en_GB`, etc.
