For now, I will patch the `KPipeline` constructor to map iso language codes to the appropriate 1-letter `lang_code`.'}, {'user': 'ROBERT-MCDOWELL', 'created_at': '2025-02-03T21:32:23Z', 'body': 'ok thanks. for eng, en-us and en-uk can be aliases of a and b indeed.. fr-ca for french canadian, fr-fr for french france....'}, {'user': 'hexgrad', 'created_at': '2025-02-04T02:39:08Z', 'body': "You can now use `en-us` and `en-gb`. I don't think `en-uk` is a legal code.

[SIWIS](https://datashare.ed.ac.uk/handle/10283/2353) is the only French voice, and that's `fr-fr`, so `fr-ca` is not supported.

Aliases listed here, as you can see they still map to the 1-letter codes internally—we're taking baby steps:

https://github.com/hexgrad/kokoro/blob/43bc156514cbb976b29c17e08d4a14d35181c7df/kokoro/pipeline.py#L11-L21"}, {'user': 'ROBERT-MCDOWELL', 'created_at': '2025-02-04T02:50:40Z', 'body': 'yes, en-gb was the right to go.... thanks!'}]
satisfaction_conditions: Support for ISO-standard language codes as input parameters
Elimination of the need for custom mapping layers between standard codes and internal implementation
Acknowledgment and commitment to address the standards compliance issue

title: Very large text with pronunciation helper fails
body:
For short text this works fine but for very long text (my test was 40k chars, so a chapter of a book) the pronunciation hint in the form of

`[Kokoro](/kˈOkəɹO/)
`
is ignored. It will pronounce BOTH the first and second parts. Again, this only occurs on extremely long text inputs and the workaround is manually splitting the text and running it separately for each part.
author: travisapple
comments:
[{'user': 'hexgrad', 'created_at': '2025-02-03T09:52:35Z', 'body': "Is your text 40k chars with no newlines? The default behavior is to split on newlines:
https://github.com/hexgrad/kokoro/blob/2f4d94bba25dc73e05ec4a9ffdee72f1d46fdd5c/kokoro/pipeline.py#L233-L240

Either way will take a look at this, but another fix in the meantime is to reach into the `G2P` class and directly override the gold lexicon like this:
```py
pipelines = {lang_code: KPipeline(lang_code=lang_code, model=False) for lang_code in 'ab'}
pipelines['a'].g2p.lexicon.golds['kokoro'] = 'kˈOkəɹO'
pipelines['b'].g2p.lexicon.golds['kokoro'] = 'kˈQkəɹQ'
```
https://huggingface.co/spaces/hexgrad/Kokoro-TTS/blob/136465fbffad342a1de9e44cc326ea75090a1828/app.py#L13-L15

Recommend you only do that for proper nouns, and still use the Markdown syntax for common words or homographs."}, {'user': 'travisapple', 'created_at': '2025-02-03T10:07:06Z', 'body': "It's 40k WITH newlines. Never more than ~300 chars per paragraph but sometimes it will split by sentence. Splitting by sentence doesn't seem to affect this issue.

Some context, I want a book reader. The book has some wild character names and so I do a search and replace on these names with pronunciations.

I'll take a hard look at the G2P options in the morning and THANK YOU for your time"}, {'user': 'hexgrad', 'created_at': '2025-02-03T10:20:00Z', 'body': "Interesting, a failure is bad either way, but 40k _with_ newlines is more concerning. To help debug, if you could supply either of the following:
```py
text = '40k chars'
longest_paragraph = max(text.split('\n'), key=len)

print(longest_paragraph)      # <= if you can share the text
print(len(longest_paragraph)) # <= if the text is copyrighted
```
If the text is copyrighted, sensitive, etc no sweat, just the length is fine in that case.

Edit: Actually on second thought, the specific paragraph (with the Markdown syntax that is double-read) causing the failure would be most helpful. title: False claim of 1000+ reasons but actually 25 only
body:
I noticed, in the README file, it is written that the reasons.json file contains 1000+ universal reasons for saying no.
I went to check that and to my surprise, there were 1001 sentences but only 25 unique ones repeated again and again!
I counted using Gemini and here are the unique ones. Add more interesting reasons as I was curious to actually read 1000 of them.
Thanks

"My inner peace committee vetoed this idea unanimously."

"I respect the opportunity, but I know my limits—and this would stretch them too far."

"Please know that my decision isn’t a reflection of you—just my own boundaries."

"That’s not something I can prioritize at the moment."

"I’ve learned to protect my time, and this doesn’t align with how I want to spend it."

"I’ve decided to hold off on new engagements for the time being."

"You’ve put great energy into this, and I hope you understand my decision to step back."

"I’m not in a position to commit to this right now."

"I'd love to say yes, but I just made a commitment to do less questionable things this week."

"Thanks for thinking of me, but I’ll have to pass on this one."

"It’s not a no forever, but it’s a no for now."

"I once made a similar decision and my cat hasn’t looked me in the eye since. Let’s not repeat history."

"Saying no to this helps me say yes to something that matters more to me."

"I truly value our connection, and I hope my no doesn’t change that."

"It sounds interesting, but I’m not the best person for this."

"I want to be honest with you—I don’t feel comfortable committing to this."

"At this point, I don’t have the bandwidth to do this justice."

"I’ve taken some time to reflect, and I believe passing on this is the right call for now."

"I'm trying to be more intentional with what I agree to, and this doesn’t quite fit."

"I’m going to respectfully decline. It doesn’t align with where I’m heading."

"I know how much this matters, but I can’t give it the attention it deserves."

"I appreciate the thought, but it’s not the right fit for me right now."

"If I said yes, I'd be lying to both of us—and my therapist said to stop doing that."

"This feels like something Future Me would yell at Present Me for agreeing to."

"This one doesn’t feel quite right, so I’ll have to pass."

title: Please publish images to GHCR
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Docker Hub has a rate limit for pulling images. Publishing to GHCR helps homelab users, and other users, who don't have paid accounts, and may run up against the pull limit.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Automate builds publishing to ghcr.io

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
N/A

**Additional context**
This projects "Issues" history suggests that this is implemented, but I do not believe that it is. It is confusing.

title: [Bug]: Documents are not processed and RAG-Chat doesn´t work correctly.
body:
### 🔍 Bug Summary

No Processed, Weired RAG-Chat

### 📖 Description

I have the problem that although I was able to upload many documents with paperless-ngx and assign them appropriate tags that are helpful for searching, when connected to paperless-AI, only the documents in paperless-ngx are recognized but not processed, i.e., they are displayed with the status “unprocessed.” Due to the lack of processing, I can neither select a document from the Manual menu item nor from Chat, and when I ask a question about an existing document in the RAG chat, the AI gives an answer that has nothing to do with the question. The AI takes any document sources and fantasizes about something that has nothing to do with the question.

My guess is that something is wrong with the indexing or with embeddings.

Paperless-NGX and Paperless-AI run on Ubuntu 24 via the Docker container Portainer.io.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

It could be that this error can only be reproduced on my system under certain unknown conditions, which is why I cannot provide exact steps to reproduce it.
I have not been able to find anyone else with the same bug report in the forum.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Documents should actually be processed and therefore selectable in paperless AI and correctly processed with AI.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

I have the problem that although I was able to upload many documents with paperless-ngx and assign them appropriate tags that are helpful for searching, when connected to paperless-AI, only the documents in paperless-ngx are recognized but not processed, i.e., they are displayed with the status “unprocessed.” Due to the lack of processing, I can neither select a document from the Manual menu item nor from Chat, and when I ask a question about an existing document in the RAG chat, the AI gives an answer that has nothing to do with the question. The AI takes any document sources and fantasizes about something that has nothing to do with the question.

My guess is that something is wrong with the indexing or with embeddings.


### 🏷️ Paperless-AI Version

1.0

title: [Bug]: "PROCESS_PREDEFINED_DOCUMENTS=yes" severely broken, causes crash, no processing
body:
### 🔍 Bug Summary

"PROCESS_PREDEFINED_DOCUMENTS=yes" severely broken, causes crash, no processing

### 📖 Description

When setting "PROCESS_PREDEFINED_DOCUMENTS=yes" it causes the document processing to completely stop and the webservice crashes, reboots when opneing the "Manual" and "Chat" pages.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up fresh paperless-ai with paperless-ngx and ollama properly configured.
2. Set above mentiones option. Option "TAGS" can be filled or empty, same result.
3. Paperless-ui will not start processing.
4. Klick "Manual" or "Chat" in the menu and webservice crashes.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Document processing should work with above mentioned options.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Service crashes, restarts.

### 🏷️ Paperless-AI Version

3.0.7

### 🔍 Bug Summary

### 📖 Description

title: [Bug]: paperless-ai not editing the paperless document
body:
### 🔍 Bug Summary

paperless-ai processes document without editing the paperless document

### 📖 Description

I just installed it a couple of days ago. And i let it run trough all my documents. It processed all 400 documents but did not  edit all of them in paperless. at the beginning there were over a 100 documends that had nothing changed to them but had an entry in the history with totally different tags and name and so on. 
I let it run a couple of times after that with tags so that i only processes the unedited documents. I even deleted the history but there are allways multiple documents that do not get edited. 
Currently i brought it down to 13 documents that are not beeing eidted by paperless-ai.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. have many documents in paperless
2. run the processing
3. look at the processed documents.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

process and edit all the documents

### ❌ Actual Behavior

edit all the  documents it processes

### 🏷️ Paperless-AI Version

3.0.7

title: Keyboard shortcuts don't work
body:
Hey @panphora,

When using the `overtype.esm.js` file, keyboard shortcuts don't seem to be working. I traced it down to the `handleAction()` function on line 2789. I don't quite get why this function is defined twice but if I replace the logic with the way the one on line 1638 works, the keyboard shortcuts work as expected.

I'm initializing the editor like so:

```javascript
<script type="module">
  import OverType, { toolbarButtons } from 'overtype.esm.js';

  const editor = new OverType('#editor', {
    autofocus: true,
    autoResize: true,
    padding: '0px',
    placeholder: "A minimum of 100 characters is required.",
    toolbar: true,
    toolbarButtons: [
      toolbarButtons.bold,
      toolbarButtons.italic,
      toolbarButtons.separator,
      toolbarButtons.bulletList,
      toolbarButtons.orderedList,
      toolbarButtons.separator,
      toolbarButtons.quote,
      toolbarButtons.separator,
      toolbarButtons.viewMode
    ]
  });
</script>
```
author: travisbell
comments:
[{'user': 'panphora', 'created_at': '2025-12-13T13:16:01Z', 'body': 'Fixed in v2.1.1!

## What was happening

You're right that `handleAction()` appeared twice - once in `Toolbar` and once in `ShortcutsManager`. The problem was they expected different inputs:

- **Toolbar's `handleAction()`** expected a button config object with an `.action` function
- **ShortcutsManager's `handleAction()`** was sending a string like `"toggleBold"`

So when you pressed Ctrl+B, the shortcut manager sent `"toggleBold"` to the toolbar, which tried to call `"toggleBold".action()` - and failed silently.

## How we fixed it

I created a single action dispatcher (`performAction`) that both toolbar clicks and keyboard shortcuts use:

1. Each toolbar button now has an `actionId` (e.g., `"toggleBold"`)
2. The editor maintains a map of `actionId → action function`
3. Both toolbar clicks and shortcuts call `editor.performAction(actionId)`

This also means **shortcuts now work even if you customize the toolbar** - they're no longer tied to which buttons are visible.

Thanks for the detailed bug report and for tracing it down to the right area!'}]
satisfaction_conditions: A solution that restores keyboard shortcut functionality when using the ESM module version
Resolution of the architectural inconsistency between duplicate function implementations
A technical explanation of the root cause of the malfunction

title: Question: Alert Dialog - temporarily disable escape key behavior?
body:
Thank you, @hunvreus, for creating Basecoat! I'm really enjoying it.

I've incorporated the [Alert Dialog](https://basecoatui.com/components/alert-dialog/) component into an app. When a user clicks the 'Continue' button, a 'delete' request is sent to the app's server. The app disables the 'Continue' and 'Cancel' buttons to indicate that the request is in progress.

However, I've encountered an issue where a user might (accidentally) press the escape key, causing Basecoat to hide the dialog while the request is still ongoing. This could lead to confusion - the user may believe he has cancelled the request.

Is there a way to temporarily disable the behavior of the escape key (i.e., hiding the dialog) while some other event occurs (such as an ongoing 'delete' request)?

title: Empty tools list when calling tools/list method
body:
### Question

When client calls the server with:
```
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/list",
  "params": {
    "cursor": "optional-cursor-value"
  }
}
```

If there are no tools returned back for that server then the expected response that the client looks for is:
```
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "tools": [],
  }
}
```

But if we look at the [json serialization spec from proto](https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/json/), it expects that tool is not added as part of the response.
So the standard serialization would return back something like this:  

```
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": { }
}
```

But we get an error from client 

```
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for ListToolsResult\n      | tools\n      |   Field required
```

Wondering if we can follow the protobuf spec and not expect the tools to be present?
Thank you. 

### Additional Context

_No response_

title: [About the σ-VAE]
body:
Thanks for nice work.

I have a question about the details of σ-VAE training.

Following the paper (Multimodal Latent Language Modeling with Next-Token Diffusion), 

I trained some σ-VAE speech tokenizer models before. 

I used fixed std of 0.5, however, I found VibeVoice used Gaussian type of std for acoustic tokenizer.

```
        if dist_type == 'fix':
            x = self.mean + self.std * torch.randn_like(self.mean)
            return x, self.std
        elif dist_type == 'gaussian':
            batch_size = self.mean.size(0)
            value = self.std / 0.8
            std = torch.randn(batch_size, device=self.mean.device, dtype=self.mean.dtype) * value

            while std.dim() < self.mean.dim():
                std = std.unsqueeze(-1)

            x = self.mean + std * torch.randn_like(self.mean)
            return x, std
        else:
            return self.mean, self.std
```

[Q1. Why do VibeVoice sample twice from a Gaussian distribution even with a fixed std?]

In my understanding, the original σ-VAE used a fixed type of std with only a single sampling. Is that correct?

[Q2. KL loss weights during training]

The paper does not provide the weight of KL loss. Which KL weight do you use during VAE training?

When using this weight, how does it affect the scale of latent representations. 

I would also like to understand the trade-off between reconstruction and generation quality as the KL weight changes.

Thank you for nice work again!

[Q1] Why do VibeVoice sample twice from a Gaussian distribution even with a fixed std?
A: In LatentLM, we've used gaussian sampling (see Eq.5) in [LatentLM paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2412.08635). The reason is that autoregressive (AR) generation introduces sampling uncertainty, and the variance of latent representations impacts next-token diffusion performance. Larger variance makes the model more robust to exposure bias during inference (see LatentLM paper, Fig. 6). By introducing variable variance during training, σ-VAE learns to operate under different uncertainty levels. This is particularly beneficial for AR models because uncertainty is not uniform across positions: earlier tokens are more uncertain, while later tokens become more deterministic as context accumulates. Training with sampled variance improves robustness across this spectrum.

[Q2] KL loss weights during training
A: When the variance is not learnable, KL Loss will degenerate into MSE loss, whose weight is 1e-2."}, {'user': 'sh-lee-prml', 'created_at': '2025-09-01T13:21:08Z', 'body': '@pengzhiliang 

Thanks for pointing that out. I had misunderstood sigma-VAE. Really appreciate your clarification!

'}]
satisfaction_conditions: Explanation of the rationale behind using variable variance sampling in the VAE architecture
Clarification of how the sampling approach relates to the theoretical framework of σ-VAE
Explanation of the relationship between variance learnability and KL loss behavior

  connections: {
    "When clicking Test": {
      main: [[{node: "Set Node A", type: "main", index: 0}]]
    }
  }
})

Result: ✅ Workflow created successfully (e.g., ID: qwzigvbMpEOhjBBm)

Step 2: Test validation mode (PASSES)

n8n_update_partial_workflow({
  id: "qwzigvbMpEOhjBBm",
  operations: [{type: "updateName", name: "TEST_RENAMED"}],
  validateOnly: true
})

Result: ✅

{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Validation successful. Operations are valid but not applied.",
  "data": {"valid": true, "operationsToApply": 1}
}

Step 3: Test actual execution (FAILS)

n8n_update_partial_workflow({
  id: "qwzigvbMpEOhjBBm",
  operations: [{type: "updateName", name: "TEST_RENAMED"}]
})

Result: ❌

{
  "success": false,
  "error": "Invalid request: request/body must NOT have additional properties",
  "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
  "details": {"message": "request/body must NOT have additional properties"}
}

Comprehensive Test Matrix

Operation Type | validateOnly: true | validateOnly: false/absent -- | -- | -- updateName | ✅ PASS | ❌ FAIL updateNode | ✅ PASS | ❌ FAIL addNode (single) | ✅ PASS | ⚠️ Partial (applies but fails validation) addNode + addConnection | ✅ PASS | ❌ FAIL addConnection alone | ✅ PASS | ❌ FAIL removeConnection | ✅ PASS | ❌ FAIL

All operation types fail with the identical error message when actually executed.

Root Cause Analysis

The error "request/body must NOT have additional properties" indicates that n8n's API is receiving a request body with properties it doesn't recognize.

Hypothesis

The MCP server's execution path is likely:

  1. Fetch current workflow from n8n API ✅
  2. Apply diff operations locally ✅
  3. Send modified workflow to n8n API ❌

At step 3, extra properties (possibly operations, validateOnly, intent, or internal MCP metadata) appear to be included in the request body sent to n8n's PUT /api/v1/workflows/{id} endpoint.

Evidence Supporting This Hypothesis

  1. Validation works perfectly - The local diff-application logic is correct
  2. All operation types fail identically - The bug is not in operation handling but in the final API call
  3. Error is from n8n API - The "request/body must NOT have additional properties" error format matches n8n's OpenAPI validation responses
  4. n8n API only accepts specific properties - name, nodes, connections, settings, active, tags

Expected Behavior

n8n_update_partial_workflow({
  id: "workflow-id",
  operations: [{type: "updateName", name: "New Name"}]
})

Should:

  1. Fetch current workflow
  2. Apply the updateName operation
  3. Send PUT /api/v1/workflows/{id} with body containing ONLY valid workflow properties
  4. Return updated workflow

Actual Behavior

Step 3 fails because the request body contains additional properties that n8n's API rejects.

Workaround

Use n8n_update_full_workflow instead:

// 1. Get current workflow
const workflow = n8n_get_workflow({id: "workflow-id", mode: "full"});

// 2. Modify as needed (manually apply changes)
workflow.name = "New Name";

// 3. Update with full replacement
n8n_update_full_workflow({
  id: "workflow-id",
  name: workflow.name,
  nodes: workflow.nodes,
  connections: workflow.connections
});

This works reliably but defeats the purpose of having efficient partial updates.

Suggested Fix Location

Based on the architecture, the bug is likely in one of these files:

  • src/mcp/handlers/n8n-update-partial-workflow.ts (or similar)
  • src/services/n8n-api.ts (or the API client layer)

The fix should ensure that when calling the n8n API after applying diff operations, only these properties are included in the request body:

  • name
  • nodes
  • connections
  • settings
  • active
  • tags

Any MCP-specific properties (operations, validateOnly, continueOnError, intent, internal metadata) must be stripped before the API call.

Impact

  • Severity: High - Core functionality is broken
  • Affected Users: All users attempting to use partial workflow updates
  • Workaround Available: Yes (n8n_update_full_workflow)

Additional Context

Documentation Discrepancy (Minor)

The README and tools_documentation show different property names for connections:

  • README: sourcePort, targetPort
  • tools_documentation: sourceOutput, targetInput

However, this is NOT the cause of the bug - both formats fail identically in execution mode while passing in validation mode.

Related Issue

This may be related to Issue #327 (addConnection syntax), but the root cause is different. Issue #327 was about syntax confusion; this issue is about the API call failing regardless of syntax.

Version Information

n8n-MCP: 2.28.3
Node.js: v22.18.0
Platform: win32
MCP Mode: stdio
n8n API: Connected successfully

From n8n_health_check({mode: "diagnostic"}):

{
  "versionInfo": {
    "current": "2.28.3",
    "latest": "2.28.3",
    "upToDate": true
  },
  "apiConfiguration": {
    "configured": true,
    "status": {"connected": true}
  }
}

title: n8n_create_workflow fails with Zod validation error in v2.26.5 HTTP mode
body:
Description:
## Bug Report

### Version
- n8n-mcp: v2.26.5

### Environment
- MCP Mode: HTTP (USE_FIXED_HTTP=true)
- n8n API: Connected and accessible

### Issue
When attempting to create workflows via `n8n_create_workflow` in HTTP mode, the operation fails with a Zod validation error.

### Error Message
{
"success": false,
"error": "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '_zod')"
}

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Set up n8n-mcp v2.26.5 in HTTP mode
2. Configure environment variables:
   - MCP_MODE=http
   - USE_FIXED_HTTP=true
   - N8N_API_URL=<your-n8n-url>
   - N8N_API_KEY=<your-api-key>
3. Call n8n_create_workflow with valid workflow structure
4. Observe the Zod validation error

### Attempted Solutions
- Set VALIDATION_PROFILE=ai-friendly - does not resolve
- Set N8N_STRICT_VALIDATION=false - does not resolve
- Set MCP_DISABLE_VALIDATION=true - does not resolve
- Set SKIP_SCHEMA_VALIDATION=true - does not resolve

### Workaround
Downgrading to v2.22.17 resolves the issue completely. Workflow creation works without any errors in HTTP mode.

### Expected Behavior
Workflow creation should succeed in v2.26.5 HTTP mode, just as it does in v2.22.17.

### Additional Context
- This appears to be a regression introduced between v2.22.17 and v2.26.5
- The error suggests undefined Zod schema references in the n8n API client validation layer
- HTTP mode environment variables for validation control are not being applied before Zod validation occurs

comments: [{'user': 'ianmurrays', 'created_at': '2025-11-28T08:29:41Z', 'body': 'Same here 🥲 ```json { "success": false, "error": "Workflow validation failed", "details": { "errors": [ "Invalid node at index 0: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '_zod')" ] } } ```'}, {'user': 'oliharvey', 'created_at': '2025-11-28T17:05:53Z', 'body': 'I downgraded my local n8n instance to Version 1.121.1 (about 9 days old) - which didn't help - so possibly it's not a recent n8n change that's broken things. --- I tried using the docker image instead of npx, but that didn't work either --- I downgraded the docker image to 2.26.4, but that didn't help --- this error itself does not seem to be present if I use 2.26.2 - however I'm seeing "Workflow validation failed" at least a bit - claude is trying to correct itself....'}, {'user': 'devangkantharia', 'created_at': '2025-11-28T17:15:44Z', 'body': 'I got a hacky workaround on the current version release v2.26.5. So, I am sending the steps until the exact solution is not patched. I have been trying n8n-mcp since last 4 days, but with all the versions I faced the same problem until I rolled my sleeves and thought of finding solution. I did using local development steps on my windows machine: ``` The following steps were done on `"D:\"` drive # 1. Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/czlonkowski/n8n-mcp.git cd n8n-mcp # 2. Install and build npm install npm run build # 3. Initialize database npm run rebuild # 4. Start the server npm start # stdio mode for Claude Desktop npm run start:http # HTTP mode for remote access ``` First, in step 4, I got few errors which didn't allow me to do `npm run start:http` So, I installed cross-env with below changes in `package.json`: ```{ ... "scripts": { "start:http": "cross-env MCP_MODE=http node dist/mcp/index.js", "start:http:fixed": "cross-env MCP_MODE=http USE_FIXED_HTTP=true node dist/mcp/index.js", "start:n8n": "cross-env N8N_MODE=true MCP_MODE=http node dist/mcp/index.js", }, ... { "devDependencies": { ... "cross-env": "^10.1.0", ... } ``` After that I could do all the 3 commands: `start:http`, `start:http:fixed`, `start:n8n` Now here is the hacky part: Firstly, I installed n8n-mcp globally: `npm install -g n8n-mcp` Secondly, I deleted `"C:\Users\\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\n8n-mcp\"` and copied complete `"D:\n8n-mcp"` here. > (Around 1.72gb) sorry :( Thirdly, in `claude_desktop_config.json` added these key-values: ``` { "mcpServers": { "n8n-mcp": { "command": "npx", "args": [ "n8n-mcp" ], "env": { "MCP_MODE": "stdio", "LOG_LEVEL": "error", "DISABLE_CONSOLE_OUTPUT": "true", "N8N_API_URL": "http://localhost:5678", "N8N_BASE_URL": "http://localhost:5678", "N8N_API_KEY": "" } } } } ``` > And Volla, it worked!!! I hope this helps!!! Sorry for this long detailed steps, I wanted to help everyone who are new with this process. '}, {'user': 'oshalabi', 'created_at': '2025-11-28T21:57:45Z', 'body': '**This fix is inspired by @devangkantharia's fix.** I managed to resolve this issue and get the MCP server running successfully in Docker. Here is the complete solution for anyone else facing the Zod validation or "no such file" errors: 1. Fix Environment Variables (The Zod Issue) As suggested, I used cross-env to handle environment variables correctly. - Installed cross-env as a dev dependency. - Updated the scripts in package.json: ``` "start:http": "cross-env MCP_MODE=http node dist/mcp/index.js", "start:http:fixed": "cross-env MCP_MODE=http USE_FIXED_HTTP=true node dist/mcp/index.js", "start:n8n": "cross-env N8N_MODE=true MCP_MODE=http node dist/mcp/index.js", ``` 2. Fix Missing Runtime Dependencies This was the main cause of the **_Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '_zod') error_**. The runtime image was missing several packages. I had to add them to package.runtime.json: ``` "dependencies": { // ... existing dependencies "cross-env": "^10.1.0", "n8n": "^1.121.2", "n8n-core": "^1.120.1", "n8n-workflow": "^1.118.1", "openai": "^4.77.0", "zod": "^3.24.1" } ``` 3. Fix Docker on Windows (CRLF Line Endings) Note: _If you are building on Windows follow this step, otherwise you can skip it._ If you are building the Docker image on Windows, the entrypoint scripts often fail with no such file or directory because of Windows line endings (\r\n). I added this to the Dockerfile to automatically fix them: ``` # In the runtime stage, replace the chmod line with this: RUN sed -i 's/\r$//' /usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/n8n-mcp && \ chmod +x /usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/n8n-mcp ``` 4. Build & Configuration Since these changes are local, you need to build your own image and tell your MCP client to use it instead of pulling from the registry. - **Build the image**: `docker build -t n8n-mcp-server .` - **Update** mcp_config.json **for your AI application**: ``` "n8n-mcp": { "command": "docker", "args": [ "run", "--pull=never", "-i", "--rm", "--init", "-e", "MCP_MODE=stdio", "-e", "LOG_LEVEL=error", "-e", "DISABLE_CONSOLE_OUTPUT=true", "-e", "N8N_API_URL=", "-e", "N8N_API_KEY=", "-e", "WEBHOOK_SECURITY_MODE=moderate", "-e", "USE_FIXED_HTTP=true", "n8n-mcp-server:latest" ] } ``` '}, {'user': 'czlonkowski', 'created_at': '2025-11-28T23:52:44Z', 'body': 'root cause found, I am working on a fix --- ## ✅ Fix Released This issue has been fixed in **v2.27.0**. ### Root Cause The `package.json` declared `"@modelcontextprotocol/sdk": "^1.20.1"` which allowed npm to resolve to SDK 1.23.0. That version accepts `"zod": "^3.25 || ^4.0"`, causing npm to deduplicate to Zod v4. SDK 1.23.0's `isZ4Schema()` function crashes when called with undefined, which happens for plain JSON Schema objects. ### Fix Applied - Pinned MCP SDK to exact version `1.20.1` - Pinned Zod to exact version `3.24.1` - Added CI workflow to prevent regression ### Availability - **npm**: `npm install n8n-mcp@2.27.0` (available in ~15 minutes) - **Docker**: Already available - `docker pull ghcr.io/czlonkowski/n8n-mcp:latest` Thank you for reporting this issue!'}]

title: Add the overlay problem on Linux and its fix on the main page
body:
As pointed in my [comment in #327](https://github.com/cjpais/Handy/issues/327#issuecomment-3567820189), I think what seems to be a known issue, with an easy temporary solution, would deserve to be on the main page. The overlay seems to hinder pasting on Linux (debian 13, with gnome and i3 on my end at least) and there is a simple solution: set "Overlay position" to `none` in the settings, in the "Advanced" submenu. Not knowing this make the app unusable, which is a pity, as the trick to overcome this is very simple and can even be compensated with the "Audio feedback".

I stumbled on the solution in a [comment on a closed issue](https://github.com/cjpais/Handy/issues/138#issuecomment-3409195540) and I think the issue may also be related to the more general problem of how to paste in Linux (see #87). I have noticed Handy seems to not use fast input on my debian 13 with Xorg, which cause it to be less smooth and create also problems when using post-processing.
